lesson.content:
## What it is
The application layer provides users with access to network services. Most applications follow the client-server model, where a server runs continuously and waits for requests, while a client starts communication, sends a request, and receives a response. [p. 2]

## Real-life analogy
Imagine a restaurant where the kitchen (server) prepares food and the customers (clients) order from the menu. The kitchen is always ready to serve, and customers place orders, which are processed and delivered. [p. 2]

## How it works
1. A client starts the communication by sending a request to a server. [p. 2]
2. The server processes the request and sends a response back to the client. [p. 2]
3. The client receives the response and can take action based on the response, such as displaying a web page or receiving an email. [p. 2]

## Key terms
- **Client-server model**: A model where a server runs continuously and waits for requests from clients, which then send requests and receive responses. [p. 2]
- **DNS (Domain Name System)**: A system that maps domain names to IP addresses, allowing users to use domain names instead of IP addresses. [p. 2]

## Example
A simple example of the client-server model in action is a web browser. When you type a URL into your browser, the client (your browser) sends a request to the server (a web server) to fetch a web page. The server processes the request, retrieves the web page, and sends it back to the client. [p. 2]

## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 2]

## Exam tip
Describe the client-server model and provide an example of how it works in a real-world application. [p. 2]
